polymer.basis: Classification and typical values from polymer handbooks and resin data sheets, as compiled for the estimate model (docs/audits/2026-09-15-filtering-estimates-data/physics/). The document cited prints a density inside the range, not its ends. NatureWorks Ingeo 3D850 (R-NATUREWORKS-INGEO-3D850-TDS), a PLA grade for 3D-printing monofilament, prints a specific gravity of 1.24 (ASTM D792), a peak melt temperature of 165-180 °C and a glass transition temperature of 55-60 °C (both ASTM D3418), p. 1. It prints no water absorption. PLA is semicrystalline and prints amorphous (D158): the melting point column holds 165 °C, the low end of the printed range, a ceiling every grade of the range stays under. The same page says that annealing "in the range of 176-266°F (80-130°C) can be used to promote crystallization": the annealing threshold is the glass transition's low end, 55 °C, at or below which nothing crystallises (D158).

polymerEnvironment.conditions: 10 % wt/vol mixture, shaken at 175 rpm at room temperature; some samples stirred at 65 °C
polymerEnvironment.finding: Of the solvents studied, chloroform is the best solvent for quickly preparing 10 % wt/vol solutions of all Ingeo grades and morphologies; 4032D pellets and injection-moulded bars were readily transformed to 10 % wt/vol solutions in chloroform in 2-4 hours at room temperature
polymerEnvironment.notes: Study grades: 4060D (12 % D, amorphous), 2003D (4.5 % D) and 4032D (1.6 % D, crystallisable) as pellets and injection-moulded bars; no filament grade was tested. A printed part is largely amorphous, so the amorphous-bar results are the nearer case. The reference reports dissolution; the verdict word "soluble" is reserved for water, so dissolution in an organic solvent is recorded as not-resistant.

polymerEnvironment.finding: 4060D fully dissolved at room temperature. polymerEnvironment.finding: Ingeo biopolymers will burn. Clear to white smoke is produced when product burns. Toxic fumes are released under conditions of incomplete combustion.
polymerEnvironment.locator: p. 4 Safety and Handling Considerations, Combustibility
polymerEnvironment.notes: No UL 94 rating is stated. Verdict convention used in this table: burns / UL 94 HB = not-resistant, V-1 or V-2 = limited, V-0 = resistant.

polymerEnvironment.finding: In-line drying is required. A moisture content of less than 0.025 % (250 ppm) is recommended to prevent viscosity degradation. Typical drying conditions are 4 hours at 80 °C (175 °F) to a dew point of -40 °C (-40 °F).
polymerEnvironment.notes: A processing threshold (hydrolytic loss of melt viscosity), not an equilibrium water uptake; the percentage in the finding is the recommended maximum before melting.
